<?php
/**
 * A custom REST endpoint: /wp-json/books/v1/books (and /books/<slug>).
 *
 * One request returns everything a book page needs, in the shape the front end
 * wants: genre names instead of IDs, the cover with its size and alt text, and
 * no WordPress-specific wrappers such as title.rendered.
 */

if ( ! defined( 'FW' ) ) {
	die( 'Forbidden' );
}

add_action( 'rest_api_init', 'headless_books_register_endpoint' );

function headless_books_register_endpoint() {
	register_rest_route( 'books/v1', '/books', array(
		'methods'             => 'GET',
		'callback'            => 'headless_books_endpoint_list',
		'permission_callback' => '__return_true', // public, read-only
	) );

	register_rest_route( 'books/v1', '/books/(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+)', array(
		'methods'             => 'GET',
		'callback'            => 'headless_books_endpoint_single',
		'permission_callback' => '__return_true',
	) );
}

function headless_books_endpoint_list() {
	$posts = get_posts( array( 'post_type' => 'book', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'numberposts' => 100 ) );
	return rest_ensure_response( array_map( 'headless_books_endpoint_shape', $posts ) );
}

function headless_books_endpoint_single( WP_REST_Request $request ) {
	$posts = get_posts( array( 'post_type' => 'book', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'name' => $request['slug'], 'numberposts' => 1 ) );
	if ( ! $posts ) {
		return new WP_Error( 'book_not_found', __( 'No book with that slug.', 'headless-books' ), array( 'status' => 404 ) );
	}
	return rest_ensure_response( headless_books_endpoint_shape( $posts[0] ) );
}

/**
 * One book, the way the front end wants it.
 */
function headless_books_endpoint_shape( WP_Post $post ) {
	$id    = $post->ID;
	$cover = fw_get_db_post_option( $id, 'cover_image' );
	$image = is_array( $cover ) && ! empty( $cover['attachment_id'] ) ? (int) $cover['attachment_id'] : 0;
	$src   = $image ? wp_get_attachment_image_src( $image, 'large' ) : false;

	return array(
		'slug'     => $post->post_name,
		'title'    => get_the_title( $post ),
		'subtitle' => (string) fw_get_db_post_option( $id, 'subtitle', '' ),
		'author'   => (string) fw_get_db_post_option( $id, 'book_author', '' ),
		'pages'    => (int) fw_get_db_post_option( $id, 'pages', 0 ),
		'genres'   => wp_get_post_terms( $id, 'genre', array( 'fields' => 'names' ) ),
		'cover'    => $src ? array(
			'url'    => $src[0],
			'alt'    => (string) get_post_meta( $image, '_wp_attachment_image_alt', true ),
			'width'  => (int) $src[1],
			'height' => (int) $src[2],
		) : null,
		'buyUrl'   => esc_url_raw( (string) fw_get_db_post_option( $id, 'buy_url', '' ) ),
		'content'  => apply_filters( 'the_content', $post->post_content ),
	);
}
files.note: A custom REST endpoint, /wp-json/books/v1/books: one request, exactly the shape the front end wants (genre names, cover with size and alt).

<?php
/**
 * Books in GraphQL (WPGraphQL), for post types and fields made with the
 * Unyson+ Post Types and Custom Fields extensions.
 *
 * Needs the WPGraphQL plugin. Does nothing without it.
 */

if ( ! defined( 'FW' ) ) {
	die( 'Forbidden' );
}

// 1. Put the post type and the taxonomy in the GraphQL schema.
add_filter( 'fw_ext_post_types_args', 'headless_books_graphql_post_type', 10, 2 );
add_filter( 'fw_ext_post_types_taxonomy_args', 'headless_books_graphql_taxonomy', 10, 2 );

function headless_books_graphql_post_type( $args, $slug ) {
	if ( 'book' === $slug ) {
		$args['show_in_graphql']     = true;
		$args['graphql_single_name'] = 'book';
		$args['graphql_plural_name'] = 'books';
	}
	return $args;
}

function headless_books_graphql_taxonomy( $args, $slug ) {
	if ( 'genre' === $slug ) {
		$args['show_in_graphql']     = true;
		$args['graphql_single_name'] = 'genre';
		$args['graphql_plural_name'] = 'genres';
	}
	return $args;
}

// 2. Add the Book Details fields to the Book type.
add_action( 'graphql_register_types', 'headless_books_graphql_fields' );

function headless_books_graphql_fields() {
	register_graphql_object_type( 'BookCover', array(
		'description' => __( 'A book cover image.', 'headless-books' ),
		'fields'      => array(
			'url'    => array( 'type' => 'String' ),
			'alt'    => array( 'type' => 'String' ),
			'width'  => array( 'type' => 'Int' ),
			'height' => array( 'type' => 'Int' ),
		),
	) );

	// Each field reads its value with fw_get_db_post_option(), as a template would.
	$value = function ( $name ) {
		return function ( $post ) use ( $name ) {
			$v = fw_get_db_post_option( $post->databaseId, $name, '' );
			return '' === $v ? null : $v;
		};
	};

	register_graphql_fields( 'Book', array(
		'subtitle'   => array( 'type' => 'String', 'resolve' => $value( 'subtitle' ) ),
		'bookAuthor' => array( 'type' => 'String', 'resolve' => $value( 'book_author' ) ),
		'pages'      => array( 'type' => 'Int', 'resolve' => $value( 'pages' ) ),
		'buyUrl'     => array( 'type' => 'String', 'resolve' => $value( 'buy_url' ) ),
		'cover'      => array(
			'type'    => 'BookCover',
			'resolve' => function ( $post ) {
				$stored = fw_get_db_post_option( $post->databaseId, 'cover_image' );
				$id     = is_array( $stored ) && ! empty( $stored['attachment_id'] ) ? (int) $stored['attachment_id'] : 0;
				$src    = $id ? wp_get_attachment_image_src( $id, 'large' ) : false;
				if ( ! $src ) {
					return null;
				}
				return array(
					'url'    => $src[0],
					'alt'    => (string) get_post_meta( $id, '_wp_attachment_image_alt', true ),
					'width'  => (int) $src[1],
					'height' => (int) $src[2],
				);
			},
		),
	) );
}
files.note: GraphQL (WPGraphQL): puts the post type and taxonomy in the schema through the Post Types filters, and adds the Book Details fields with register_graphql_fields().

<?php
/**
 * The Book post type and the Genre taxonomy.
 *
 * `show_in_rest` is what makes them appear in the REST API at
 * /wp-json/wp/v2/book and /wp-json/wp/v2/genre.
 */

if ( ! defined( 'FW' ) ) {
	die( 'Forbidden' );
}

add_action( 'init', 'headless_books_register_types' );

function headless_books_register_types() {
	register_post_type( 'book', array(
		'labels'       => array(
			'name'          => __( 'Books', 'headless-books' ),
			'singular_name' => __( 'Book', 'headless-books' ),
		),
		'public'       => true,
		'has_archive'  => true,
		'rewrite'      => array( 'slug' => 'books' ),
		'menu_icon'    => 'dashicons-book',
		'supports'     => array( 'title', 'editor', 'excerpt', 'thumbnail' ),
		'show_in_rest' => true,
	) );

	register_taxonomy( 'genre', 'book', array(
		'labels'       => array(
			'name'          => __( 'Genres', 'headless-books' ),
			'singular_name' => __( 'Genre', 'headless-books' ),
		),
		'hierarchical' => true,
		'show_in_rest' => true,
	) );
}
files.note: Registers the Book post type and Genre taxonomy with show_in_rest, so they appear in the API.

# Headless Books — child theme

The WordPress side of a headless site, written as code instead of set up in the admin. It is a child
theme of `unysonplus-theme` and needs the Unyson+ plugin active. The parent theme loads every file in
`inc/includes/` automatically, so `functions.php` has nothing to require.

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `inc/includes/headless-books-types.php` | Registers the `book` post type and `genre` taxonomy, both in the REST API. |
| `framework-customizations/theme/options/posts/book.php` | The "Book Details" fields on the Book edit screen. |
| `inc/includes/headless-books-rest.php` | Adds those values to the REST API as `book_fields`, with the cover's size and alt text. |

Install it like any theme (zip this folder, then Appearance → Themes → Add New → Upload) and activate it.

```bash
curl "https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/book?_fields=id,slug,title,book_fields"
```

Use this route when the definitions should live in version control or ship with a theme. For a
no-code setup, the Post Types and Custom Fields extensions create the same thing from the admin.
